name: Toolbar
purpose: Style one logical group of related commands with Atom toolbar semantics and roving keyboard focus.
useWhen: Related editor or application controls should behave as one horizontal or vertical keyboard group.

avoidWhen.condition: The items are navigation destinations or unrelated standalone actions.
avoidWhen.useInstead: NavigationMenu/NavList or separate Button and IconButton controls

composition: Compose Button, Link, Group, Input, Separator and ToggleGroup/ToggleItem inside a named Root. Share Button/Toggle/Input presentation; keep one roving scope.

rules.statement: Use the shared token-only radius contract only on the public parts listed in docs/guides/radius.md. Omit it to retain the owner default; do not combine it with legacy corner shape or forward it to native elements. Core names and semantic roles are distinct; popup boundaries are independent of their triggers.
Use Toolbar rather than adding manual arrow-key handlers or role=toolbar to an AppBar row.
Load styles.css or core.css plus toolbar.css and any composed Icon stylesheet.

Use Button recipes for commands and Toggle recipes for selection. Root size supplies responsive defaults; item props override. Composed asChild/render hosts own presentation, so give IconButton its size and inside focus ring explicitly.

Keep a horizontal Input last so native editing keys remain available and Tab exits; do not add another roving scope. Root disabled dominates descendants; focusableWhenDisabled never permits activation.
Toolbar does not wrap. Bound its container for native main-axis overflow; do not hide controls or invent an overflow menu.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using AppBar.Toolbar as the behavior owner or placing unrelated page actions in one roving group.
commonMistakes.correction: Compose a named Toolbar only around logically related controls.

validation: Test orientation, arrows, disabled items, links, toggles, separators, Tab entry/exit, focus rings, touch targets, overflow, themes, zoom, and RTL.
